newsitem.title: USA: US EPA sets public hearings on air standards plan.
newsitem.headline: US EPA sets public hearings on air standards plan.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Friday set four public hearings on its proposal to strengthen air quality standards on smog and soot.
The hearings will be January 14 and 15 in Boston, Chicago and Salt Lake City, Utah, and there will be a special hearing on technical aspects on January 14 in Durham, N.C.
The EPA in November proposed strengthening the standards on smog and airborne particles or soot, saying current standards did not adequately protect public health.
Many industry groups are lobbying against the changes, saying they would require costly pollution controls that would hamper economic growth.
But environmental and health advocates said tighter standards are essential to reduce premature deaths and asthma and other lung illnesses.
The November announcement opened a two-month public comment period, and the agency is to announce a final rule in June.
Congress also is expected to hold hearings on the issue.
